title: Rational and algebraically closed coefficient twists have inverse evaluations.
statement:
The theorem `WeilConjectures.fieldTwist_inverse` has the following exact Lean type. It is the strict intermediate interface used by the parent proposition:

theorem fieldTwist_inverse
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (S : Scheme.{u})
    [∀ x : S, Invertible (l : S.residueField x)]
    (Ω : Type v) [Field Ω] [Algebra (Padic l) Ω] [IsAlgClosure (Padic l) Ω]
    (m : ℤ) :
    Nonempty (sfRationalTwistingFunctor l E S m ⋙
      sfRationalTwistingFunctor l E S (-m) ≅ 𝟭 _) ∧
    Nonempty (sfQbarTwistingFunctor l S Ω m ⋙ sfQbarTwistingFunctor l S Ω (-m) ≅ 𝟭 _)

proof.text: Choose a prime p greater than l and a finite-field datum of characteristic p. Apply tateTwist_locallyFree with an algebraic-closure embedding of E into Omega. Its field-stage clauses supply equivalences whose functor and inverse are exactly the prescribed twists at n and -n. Substitute those functor equalities into the unit and counit isomorphisms. For a nonnegative integer m use the unit inverses; for a negative integer use the counits at its positive absolute value. This gives both the rational and common-stage inverse identities, including exponent zero.

proof_origin: Proof from the existing signed Tate equivalences in det-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free; arithmetic choice of an auxiliary finite-field datum does not impose a condition on S.
